question.text: Rewrite the statement $\neg ( (A \land B) \land (A \lor \neg B) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.explanation:
De Morgan's laws state that

\[ egin{align*} eg ( A \land B) \equiv eg A \lor eg B, \[3pt] eg ( A \lor B) \equiv eg A \land eg B. \end{align*} \]

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

\[ egin{align*} eg ( (A \land B) \land (A \lor eg B) ) &\equiv eg (A \land B) \lor eg (A \lor eg B) \[3pt] &\equiv ( eg A \lor eg B) \lor ( eg A \land eg ( eg B) ) \[3pt] &\equiv ( eg A \lor eg B) \lor ( eg A \land B ) \[3pt] \end{align*} \]

question.text: Rewrite the statement $ eg ( eg M \lor (M \land eg N) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.explanation:
De Morgan's laws state that

\[ egin{align*} eg ( M \land N) \equiv eg M \lor eg N, \[3pt] eg ( M \lor N) \equiv eg M \land eg N. \end{align*} \]

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

\[ egin{align*} eg ( eg M \lor (M \land eg N) ) &\equiv eg ( eg M) \land eg (M \land eg N) \[3pt] &\equiv M \land ( eg M \lor eg ( eg N) ) \[3pt] &\equiv M \land ( eg M \lor N ) \[3pt] \end{align*} \]

question.text: Simplify the statement $\neg (Q \lor \neg R )$ using De Morgan's laws.
question.explanation:
De Morgan's laws state that

egin{align*} eg ( A \lor B) \equiv eg A \land eg B, \[3pt] eg ( A \land B) \equiv eg A \lor eg B. \end{align*}

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

egin{align*} eg ( Q \lor eg R ) &\equiv eg Q \land eg ( eg R) \[3pt] &\equiv eg Q \land R \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying a Statement Using De Morgan's Laws

question.text:
$\qquad$ $n$ is not divisible by $3$ and $n$ is not divisible by $5.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.choice1: $n$ is divisible by $3$ or $n$ is divisible by $5$
question.choice2: $n$ is divisible by $3$ or $n$ is not divisible by $5$
question.choice3: $n$ is divisible by $3$ and $n$ is not divisible by $5$
question.choice4: $n$ is not divisible by $3$ or $n$ is not divisible by $5$
question.choice5: $n$ is divisible by $3$ and $n$ is divisible by $5$
question.explanation:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

\[ \neg ( A \land B) = \neg A \lor \neg B \]

So, the negation of our statement is

\begin{align*} \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! \neg (n\textrm{ is not divisible by $3$} \textrm{ and }& n \textrm{ is not divisible by $5$})\\[5pt] &\equiv \neg \big( (n\textrm{ is not divisible by $3$}) \land (n \textrm{ is not divisible by $5$}) \big) \\[5pt] &\equiv \neg ( n\textrm{ is not divisible by $3$}) \lor \neg (n \textrm{ is not divisible by $5$}) \\[5pt] &\equiv (n\textrm{ is divisible by $3$}) \lor (n \textrm{ is divisible by $5$}) \\[5pt] &\equiv n\textrm{ is divisible by $3$} \textrm{ or } n \textrm{ is divisible by $5$}. \end{align*}

example.title: Negating a Sentence Containing a Conjunction

question.text:
$\qquad$ $2$ is not prime or $2 \not \in \mathbb{Q}.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.explanation:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

\[ \neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B \]

So, the negation of our statement is

\begin{align*} \neg \left( 2\text{ is not prime} \text{ or } 2 \not \in \mathbb{Q} \right) &\equiv \neg \left( (2\text{ is not prime}) \lor (2 \not \in \mathbb{Q}) \right) \\[5pt] &\equiv \neg \left( 2\text{ is not prime} \right) \land \neg \left( 2 \not \in \mathbb{Q} \right) \\[5pt] &\equiv (2\text{ is prime}) \land (2 \in \mathbb{Q}) \\[5pt] &\equiv 2\text{ is prime} \textrm{ and } 2 \in \mathbb{Q}. \end{align*}
